title: The Wall Tithe
about: Gunther's own story. Every village on Aldmoor pays the Wall Tithe to keep the orcs at bay. Gunther learns where the silver really goes.

prologue.title: The Wall Tithe
text: Every spring the tithe-wardens come to the villages of Aldmoor. A tenth of the grain, a tenth of the silver, and one child in ten for the levy.

text.text: The Wall Tithe. The price of keeping the clans of Skullrock in the north.

text: Three springs ago, on tithe day in Ashby, a quarry girl called Wren climbed onto the well and sang the Freeholder's Lament. The song is banned.

text.text: Hang her from the mill beam. Before sundown.

text: She found your face in the crowd.

text.text: The tithe never reaches the wall, Gunther. Ask where it goes.

text: You ran that night, with your bow and three quarry lads who would not let you go alone.

text.text: Riders on the Fairmeet road. The wardens' men. They've found us.
Then we stop running. Stand with me.

prologue.decline: Not now, I am just a sellsword
after: The wardens' men scatter into the dark.

after.text: They'll call you an outlaw now.

after: Three years pass. You sell your bow to anyone who pays, and now you lead a warband of your own.

after.text: And still nobody in Ashby will tell me where the tithe goes.

chapters.short: Ask about the Wall Tithe in Fairmeet.
chapters.title: Where the tithe goes
chapters.goal: Ask about the Wall Tithe in Fairmeet. The free city keeps no tithe-wardens, so people talk there.
scene: The tavern goes quiet when you ask. One man does not: a thin clerk with a patch over one eye, who waves you to his corner.

scene.text: Hob Carrow. I kept the tithe ledgers for the March, until I added them up.
And the eye?
That is what adding up cost me. Your friend was right, captain. The silver goes north on the Gutrot road with no guard at all, and no orc ever touches it.
Who else knows?
Clerks, carters, quarry folk. We call ourselves the Unbound. But a ledger is only ink. Bring me something nobody can argue with.
The next cart left three days ago. Orcs meet it on the road below Gutrot Camp. Take what they are carrying.

chapters.short: Take the chest from the tithe-runners near Gutrot Camp.
chapters.title: The tithe-runners
chapters.goal: Find the orc tithe-runners near Gutrot Camp and take the chest they carry. They are marked with ! on the map.

party.name: Tithe-runners
party.desc: Clan orcs hauling an iron-bound chest north to Skullrock, with no banner. They do not want to be seen.

scene: The chest is heavy with silver, stamped with the treasury marks of the Vale and the Ember March. Under the coins is a letter, sealed in grey wax with the print of a burnt oak leaf.

scene.text: To the Warlord, for the season. Raid where they grumble, spare where they pay. Burn Ashby again if it sings.
The clans are not the tithe's enemy. They are its hired hands.

scene: Someone pays Gorrak to burn villages on the border, so the villages keep paying for protection. Someone who seals their letters with a burnt leaf.

scene.text: Four hundred silver marks, captain. What do we do with it?

choices.label: Send the silver to Hob for the Unbound
text: Hob's carters take the chest by night.

text.text: Every mark goes back to a village it came from.

choices.label: Keep it. Your men need paying
text: Your men cheer when you share it out.
Hob says nothing, but he writes something in his ledger.

chapters.short: See Mother Quill, the forger in Brightwater.
chapters.title: A borrowed name
chapters.goal: Hob says the burnt leaf belongs to the Ashen Compact, a circle of highborn houses that meets in secret. To get inside it, you need a highborn name. Find Mother Quill, the forger in Brightwater. You will need to be known (renown 40) and to pay her 400 gold.
scene: Mother Quill works by one candle in a room full of old charters. She looks you over the way a horse trader looks at teeth.

scene.text: House Varn. Marsh lords, very old and very poor. The last of them drowned at sea twenty years back, and nobody went to the funeral.
And who am I?
Varn's lost nephew, raised abroad. That accounts for the manners.

scene: The writ she hands you is better than real. Hob reads it twice.

scene.text: Good. The Compact only takes new blood one way: the Proving at the Highcrag. Each year the young heirs bring their retinues to the hills and fight until one is left standing.
The winner gets a seat at the table. They have one rule, and it is not much of a rule: try not to kill each other.

chapters.short: Beat Leofric Crane's retinue at the Highcrag, west of Stonefold.
chapters.title: The Proving
chapters.goal: Win the Proving at the Highcrag, in the hills west of Stonefold. Leofric Crane, son of the Compact's chancellor, is the favourite. His retinue is marked with ! on the map.

party.name: Leofric Crane's retinue
party.desc: Highborn heirs and their sworn men, here for the Proving. Leofric Crane rides at the front in silvered mail.

scene: Leofric's men break and run. The heir fights on alone, until your blade knocks his sword into the heather.
Another heir comes whooping down the slope, covered in someone else's blood. He fought on your side for the whole of the last day, uninvited.

scene.text: Wick Ashe. Youngest son, and nobody's favourite. Well, Varn, you've won the Proving.
Now what about him?

scene: Leofric looks up at you from the mud. For a moment he looks very young. He does not beg.

choices.label: Spare him
text: You give Leofric his sword back, hilt first.
Leofric says nothing, but he does not take his eyes off your face.

choices.label: End him, as the old rules allow
text: It is quick. The heirs fall silent.
By nightfall the story has run all the way to Redcliff, and the chancellor has heard from a stranger that his only son is dead.

reward.say: Wick Ashe and his sworn sword join your warband.

chapters.short: Go to Redcliff and stand before the Ashen Compact.
chapters.title: Among wolves
chapters.goal: As victor of the Proving, you are summoned before the Ashen Compact. Go to Redcliff. The Compact only receives captains of name (renown 80).
scene: Chancellor Aurek Crane is a soft-voiced man with ink on his fingers.

scene.text: You beat my son and gave him back his life. I have not decided whether that was kindness or an insult. Sit.
The Proving is the Proving. Leofric knew the rules. Sit.
His eyes are red at the rims. He does not look at you again for the rest of the night.

scene: Round the table sit eleven highborn of the Vale and the March, the people who truly rule both crowns. The queen and Lord Brannoc know nothing of it.

scene.text: And the tithe?
Fear is the cheapest wall there is. Gorrak takes a fifth of the silver and burns a few barns, and the villages pay us for the privilege of not being burned.
Without him, they would start asking what they need lords for.
This season, House Varn will carry the tithe north. Swear it.

choices.label: Swear, and mean it for now
text: The seal is cold in your palm. On the road north the silver passes through your hands, and the Compact pays you a carrier's cut.

choices.label: Swear, and copy the tithe rolls tonight
text: That night, while the Compact sleeps off its wine, you copy the name of every house on the tithe rolls by candlelight. Hob will want them.

chapters.short: Read Gorrak's letter in three villages.
chapters.title: Rouse the bondfolk
chapters.goal: Hob wants the villages to know the truth before the Compact can silence it. Read Gorrak's letter aloud in the squares of three villages. Each one will send you men.

step.button: Read Gorrak's letter in the square
step.each: The square fills. You read the letter, and you show them the grey seal. An old woman starts to sing the Freeholder's Lament, and the whole village takes it up. Their best young people come to join you.

scene: Three villages have now heard the truth, and word runs ahead of you down every road.

scene.text: They threw mud at the wardens in Millford! And in Ashby someone cut down the mill beam where Wren died.
Master Carrow sent me with a message for you.
Well done. Now be careful. They will know it was you.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.goal: The Compact knows who you are. Its swords are coming for you. Survive them.

party.name: Leofric Crane's riders
party.desc: Leofric Crane, whose life you spared at the Highcrag, leads them. He looks sick about it.

party.name: The Chancellor's huntsmen
party.desc: Aurek Crane's household guard, sworn to avenge his son.

scene: Mother Quill sold you. A forger who sells papers will sell anything, and the Compact paid well for the name of the man behind House Varn.

scene.text: When it is over, Leofric is on his knees in the mud for the second time.
They told me you were a quarry rat. I said a quarry rat would not have spared me.
I was wrong about what quarry rats are, wasn't I?
You let him go again. This time he rides south, away from Redcliff.
Among the dead is a huntsman with a satchel full of letters. One is addressed to the chancellor.
Bad news on the last page, captain. Hob Carrow was taken in Fairmeet two nights ago.
It says he hid his ledger first, under the board where he always sat. The names, the sums and the seals of the whole Compact, in red ink.
The Red Ledger. Fairmeet's Guildmoot is the one place where every realm sits together. Read it there, and no lord on Aldmoor can pretend not to have heard.

chapters.title: The Red Ledger
chapters.goal: Recover Hob's ledger in Fairmeet and read it before the Guildmoot. The Guildmoot will only hear a captain the whole island knows (renown 140).

step.button: Read the Red Ledger to the Guildmoot

scene: The ledger is where Hob said it would be. You read it standing, page by page, while the envoys of four crowns and the free city listen.

scene.text: The sums. The seals. The villages. And the date of every burning, paid for in advance.
Then you lay your copy of the tithe rolls beside it, and the two match name for name. Nobody in the hall can call it a forgery.
The silver from Gutrot came back to my village. Every mark of it. He could have kept it.
The Vale will hear this tonight. Riders! To Brightwater, Redcliff, Elthir and Dunmar!

scene: Aurek Crane does not wait to be arrested. He gathers the Compact's households and every sellsword money can buy, and marches out of Redcliff. If he breaks you, he can still burn the ledger and everyone who heard it.
Hob Carrow's body was found in the river below Fairmeet. He never told them where the ledger was.

chapters.short: Defeat the Ashen Host near Redcliff.
chapters.title: The Ashen Host
chapters.goal: Defeat Chancellor Aurek Crane and the Ashen Host near Redcliff. It is the strongest army on the island. Gather your men first.

party.name: The Ashen Host
party.desc: The households of the Ashen Compact and their hired orcs, under the burnt-leaf banner. Chancellor Aurek Crane rides in the middle of them.

scene: The burnt-leaf banner goes down in the mud. Aurek Crane is pulled from under his horse, alive.

scene.text: You have torn down the only wall this island ever had.
It was never a wall. Take him to the Guildmoot.

scene: The crowns of Aldmoor abolish the Wall Tithe within the month. In every village square the Freeholder's Lament is sung openly for the first time in a hundred years.
Gorrak's silver has stopped. The Warlord is still up in Skullrock, and still dangerous. Now, though, the island knows exactly what he was for.
In Ashby they put up a stone by the old mill. It has Wren's name on it, and under that a line of the song. Your name is not on it.

scene.text: Good.

reward.chronicle: Gunther broke the Ashen Compact. The Wall Tithe is no more.

ending: The story of the Wall Tithe is over. The island is yours to roam: take towns, raise a family, and play the realms against each other.
